Hi Olga / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran the internal readiness check and have a few items we want to lock down before the SOW is finalized and the procurement ticket goes through next week: 1) preferred primary region (we're leaning SEA us-west but want to confirm failover), 2) burst caps — our traffic pattern has unpredictable spikes tied to nightly batch enrichment, 3) network egress constraints (we need more detail for our security team).

Attached a stamped copy of the draft SOW with our comments (haven_sow_v0.3.pdf) and a simple network diagram. Can we get a short internal decision thread that lists the region, burst policy (tokens/second ceiling + duration), and any required firewall rules? Procurement needs that to include in the PO.

Prefer to have decisions by tomorrow EOD PT. Happy to join a quick call if that speeds things up.

—Samir
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
HavenAI

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provisioning checkpoint: HavenAI GPU pool, burst guardrails and regional selection

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I pulled Ben and Priyom into this thread so we can give a consolidated response. Quick summary up-front: we can support primary us-west with automatic failover to us-east, a configurable burst cap with two policy options (short high-burst vs sustained low-burst), and a minimal set of egress/network rules we recommend. See details below and Ben's checklist for operational steps.

DECISIONS TO CONFIRM (proposal):
- Primary region: us-west-2 (Oregon). Failover: us-east-1 (N. Virginia) with DNS-based routing and health checks.
- Burst policy (choose one):
  Option A — Spike Mode: 1.2M tokens/minute for up to 3 minutes, cool-down 10 minutes, max 6 spikes/day.
  Option B — Sustained Mode: 250k tokens/minute sustained, with autoscale to 500k tokens/minute during 15-minute windows.
- Network: Allow egress to 52.53.0.0/16 and 18.205.0.0/16 (Redwood API endpoints). TLS-only. No public inbound ports required; customer VPN or SSM jump host for ops.

Ben, Priyom — can you confirm capacity lead times and which option is safer for a first-week ramp? Samir — if you prefer Option A we can reserve short-burst headroom for the first 30 days and then re-evaluate.

I'll also upload a short decision checklist to the Drive link and flag the SOW comment locations.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Customer Implementation
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-burst-policy-draft.md (MD, 6KB)

Quick ops checklist and lead times from capacity/provisioning perspective:

1) Region provisioning: us-west-2 standard dedicated pool available in 14 business days once SOW signed and initial commit provisioned. us-east-1 failover pool can be standby (warm) in 10 business days. Cross-region replication of KV cache will add ~6 business days of orchestration work.

2) Burst headroom: to support Option A (short spikes) we recommend reserving 30% additional headroom on day 1 (estimated pool: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs). For Option B (sustained) prefer 12 A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscaler configured to scale in 2-min windows.

3) Networking: we will provide a concise firewall rule list and a small NAT egress footprint. If HavenAI needs private peering, add 10 business days to setup.

4) Failover and routing: implement Route53 weighted failover + ALB health checks. We will provide runbooks and tracing hooks to validate KV cache continuity.

Next steps I recommend we do:
- Confirm Option (A or B) by EOD 7/2 PT
- Legal to accept SOW comments; procurement to issue PO by 7/5
- Redwood to kick off provisioning once PO is received; ops playbook delivered within 48h of pool creation

I can be on the call tomorrow 11am PT to finalize.

—Ben
Head of Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference

On timelines: procurement will try to get the PO out by 7/5 but may need approval from finance; I'll keep you posted. Can you confirm the A100-equivalent GPU counts for Option A reservation (Ben)? Also we asked our compliance team to review the SOW comments; they flagged a short note about log retention and audit exports — I attached the SOW with an inline comment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samir — excellent, thanks for the confirmations. Final decision summary I'm logging here for procurement and the SOW:

- Primary region: us-west-2 (Oregon). Failover: us-east-1 (N. Virginia) as warm pool with KV replication.
- Burst policy: Option A (Spike Mode) with adjusted limit: 1.2M tokens/minute for up to 3 minutes; increased to 10 spikes/day for the first 7 days; cool-down 10 minutes. Redwood will reserve 12 A100-equivalent GPUs for week-1 stabilization.
- Networking: Redwood will provide egress IP ranges and a short firewall template. HavenAI will open a managed VPN peering request (NET-4121) to support ops access.
- Compliance note: Redwood agrees to include a 90-day log retention export window and audit export hooks; detailed retention language to be added to SOW v0.4.

Next operational steps:
1) HavenAI procurement to issue PO (target 2029-07-05).
2) Once PO received, Redwood will kick off provisioning; expected pool ready in ~14 business days.
3) Priyom will run the provisioning call and hand off runbooks; staging priming prompts requested from HavenAI.

I'll update the Drive folder and attach the SOW with these decisions (haven_sow_v0.4 expected later today). If procurement slips, call Ben and I and we'll discuss temporary credit coverage.

Thanks everyone — good momentum.
Olga
